# Running the original Blitz3D in the container

The original Blitz3D 1.118 compiler and its Direct3D 7 runtime run under Wine in the Linux container, rendered by Mesa
llvmpipe on Xvfb. Use it for **functional** comparisons only (screenshots, pixel values, program output). Timing under
Wine plus software rendering is meaningless, so never quote performance numbers from it.

## One-time setup (per container)

1. The original binaries are not in the repository. Copy `blitzcc.exe`, `debugger.dll`, `linker.dll` and `runtime.dll`
   of Blitz3D 1.118 to `/mnt/project-files/blitz3d-original/bin/` (already there), or point `B3D_ORIG_BIN` at them.
2. `tools/original_blitz3d.sh setup` installs wine and wine32, a 32-bit Wine prefix at `/opt/wine32`, and the compiler at `/opt/b3d`.

## Use

`tools/original_blitz3d.sh run path/to/program.bb [timeout]` compiles with the original `blitzcc` and runs the result
with the program's directory as the working directory. Write images from the program itself with
`SaveBuffer FrontBuffer(),"shot.bmp"` after `Flip`. Output of `Print` goes to the Wine console, `DebugLog` is not visible
(release build); write values with `WriteFile` instead. Use windowed `Graphics3D w,h,32,2`, never fullscreen.

## Verified

A Graphics3D program with camera, light and a lit cube compiles and renders correctly (original Direct3D 7 through
wined3d on llvmpipe, 320x240 `SaveBuffer` output matches expectations). A compile of `cases_3b_4.bb` also works.
The same Wine/Xvfb setup is needed for any executable the original compiler produces.
